ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha 6bb672061d65 introduced a refactor to recommendation-service/scorer/batch.go that rewrote the inner scoring loop in BatchScorer.ScoreUsers(). The new implementation launches a goroutine per user in each batch but uses a bare channel select that does not include a case for ctx.Done(). When the parent request context is cancelled (e.g., due to client timeout or upstream deadline), the spawned goroutines continue blocking on feature-store I/O indefinitely instead of exiting. Under sustained load with any client-side or upstream timeouts, goroutines accumulate unboundedly, exhausting heap memory and triggering OOM kills. The bug is on line 187 of recommendation/scorer/batch.go where the select statement omits the `case <-ctx.Done(): return` branch.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately restart recommendation-service pods to temporarily reduce goroutine count (buys ~3-5 minutes before leak recurs). 2. Roll back deploy 6bb672061d65 by reverting recommendation-service/scorer/batch.go to the prior version from sha 310357e9b0b4, re-deploying — this eliminates the leak. 3. As a permanent fix, add `case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err()` to the select block in BatchScorer.ScoreUsers() at batch.go:187, and add a unit test that cancels the context mid-batch and asserts all goroutines exit within 1 second. 4. Add a goroutine count metric alert at threshold 5000 to catch future leaks earlier.
